steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: The clouds above Zwillingstürme are... floating so freely.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Is this what you wanted to see at the end?

steps.name: 'Cora'
steps.text: Ja.

steps.name: 'Cora'
steps.text: Your music helped me see. Incredible. Not through my eyes, but through my mind.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I gave Viviana a few hints, as you wished.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: She wanted so much to have a real family, but... she didn't follow her strongest emotions.

steps.name: 'Cora'
steps.text: Nein, my dear friend.

steps.name: 'Cora'
steps.text: It was her feelings for everyone that led to her decision to kill me.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Are you satisfied?

steps.name: 'Cora'
steps.text: Why wouldn't I be?

steps.name: 'Cora'
steps.text: I greeted death under the gaze of the one I loved.

steps.name: 'Cora'
steps.text: No need to mourn for me. This is the best end a sinner like me could hope for.

steps.name: 'Cora'
steps.text: Danke. Thanks to you, both Viviana and I will... go further.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Your emotions will vanish into thin air before long.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: When the music ends, the strings may continue to vibrate for a while, but all sounds eventually fade into silence.

steps.name: 'Cora'
steps.text: No one can keep a cloud around, Arturia.

steps.name: 'Cora'
steps.text: The soul is frail. Even the most powerful emotions and the greatest desires will inevitably reach their respective ends.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Even for the strongest of souls?

steps.name: 'Cora'
steps.text: Is that not what you're here for?

steps.name: 'Cora'
steps.text: I'm leaving all my emotions and memories to you. Did you find what you were looking for?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Yes, perhaps... I'll know soon.

steps.name: 'Cora'
steps.text: Goodbye, Arturia.

steps.name: 'Cora'
steps.text: I hope you find your answer in melody.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Cora Löwenstein, my gentle and stubborn friend... I was glad to have you on this journey.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I'll work to achieve the future we sought together.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: You and I...

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: ...Will meet again in melody.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Cora is... fading away?

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Get away from her!

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Herr Reiner...

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Cora...

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: There's no need to explain.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: You made your decision... and put it to action.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: As for the rest...

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: This isn't the time to speak of it, for neither of us.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: The black flame took her. It was similar to what happened at Ludwigs-Universität.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: They were both Herkunftshorn's Arts, but not quite the same.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: The caster in that incident was an imitator who activated them by force, but this power feels almost like his own.
Red-black energy rumbles in the clouds.
It does not impatiently tear, swallow, and spread.
Instead it paces, watches and waits, on that throne in the clouds.

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: Do you see it?

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: The great Herkunftshorn has heeded our call and granted us an audience!

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'
steps.text: He has called forth the staircase leading to his eternal spire, the Genesis Horn!
The followers of the Witch King laugh.
They play the most piercing notes on their instruments, aiming them at their own chests and throats.
In response, the black clouds extend several tendrils towards them.
The dying cultists kiss the hand that their king has extended and become one with the black flame, ascending to become part of the dark cloud that now hovers above the Twin Spires.
The sky cracks with a dissonant roar.
Leithanien's greatest and most terrible sovereign, Herkunftshorn, issues his edict to his people.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: ...Herkunftshorn is really back.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: We have a problem.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Bound by the Arts inherent to the Movement, the people continue to play. But the altered Güldenesgesatz now only feeds Herkunftshorn's power.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: What did you just do?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Tried to shoot the cloud.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Now's not the time for this madness.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Madness? Not at all, Lessing. Do you know how long I've waited for this moment?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I was destined for this ever since his noise was forced into my head... No, since the day I was born.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You told me to fight, to face my responsibility and sins head-on. And you were completely right. Herkunftshorn is my sin, and it's my responsibility to face him.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I just need a way to drag him down from his palace in the clouds. Or... wherever he is.
Or I could send you up?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Wha—
An invisible thread catches him by the collar. It is light, gentle, and cool.
Suddenly, it constricts.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Argh—!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Who are you?!
Rude to yell at someone who just saved your life, don't you think?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: The black flame... it landed right where I was standing?
Listen to Lessing and stop shaking your wand at the clouds. He can be a little stiff, but he's more reliable than most.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: That was awfully sudden, Ermengarde.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Were you expecting a schedule? A timetable? I rushed all the way back from Kazdel. Look how much wear and tear there is on my cube-thing.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: My hat got all dirty, too. Mind if I clean it with your horn?

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: You're no fun.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Just... keep your hands off my horns. How bad is the situation?

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Extremely.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: I don't even need witchcraft to tell you that much. This place is filled with threads that don't belong to it. It's so messy not even a Lich could clean it up. A little rain wouldn't solve anything.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Are you a Lich too?

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Do I not look the part?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I thought...

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: You thought Liches were all old men with long white beards, dressed in robes covering head to tail, with skeletal staves in their hands?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: ...I thought Liches would have more refined vocabularies.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: What happened to the old man?

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: You know the first thing about him, don't you? Of course he went straight into that cloud.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: He strode back from the border of Leithanien the moment Herkunftshorn opened his eyes on the throne.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: And he pulled on all our threads, too. I'm sure even the Liches of Kazdel could hear his cursing.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: How many of you are here?

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Everyone who could come.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Do you realize how inconvenient this is? It's like you were planning to move, and had loaded all your scrolls and talismans on the truck, then the very next day you hear that your old home is getting blown up.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: I mean, can't you Leithanians keep things together for even a single day without us?

spans.text: I mean, can't you Leithanians keep things together for even

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: The Liches are back.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: ...This is a serious situation.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: The Genesis Horn is about to descend.

steps.name: Michael
steps.text: Grimmacht, your violin...

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: Good.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: We haven't played together in a while, Lieselotte.

steps.name: Ewigegnade
steps.text: Ja. The ensemble performance should be coming to a close, as is the custom. Then it's our turn.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: Herkunftshorn... the calamity that Leithanien has always been destined to face.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: We already beat him once.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: We can do it again.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: It's the Kaiserinnen's melody.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Grimmacht and Ewigegnade have made their move.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: Do what you need to, Viviana.

steps.name: Gesatzswächter
steps.text: ...We'll do our part as well.
Golden light floods out from the Gesatzswächter's sword and armor.
As the light engulfs him, the other Gesatzswächter respond to the empresses' melody.
Beams of Arts shoot towards the sky from every corner, drawing closer together and joining up.
The sky is covered in black, but an even brighter cloud rises from the ground.
Under the golden arch, the sound of an organ gently covers those beneath the Twin Spires, while the violin's passionate, soaring notes pierce the roiling clouds like a sword.
Dozens of hands weave thousands of threads, plucking at the melody in the sky and the wind, making them even clearer.
The Twin Empresses, the Gesatzswächter, and the Liches.
All the guardians of Leithanien stand together against its former king, now returning from the void.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The chaos grows.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Only the Kaiserinnen's melody can fight Herkunftshorn.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Melody?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Organ, violin... and cello.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I can't hear the cello.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: It's a part of the noise. Not at all like ordinary music.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Your ears are accustomed to hearing music, but mine are equally receptive to all forms of sound.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The conclusion is clear.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Arturia has escaped from prison.

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'?
steps.text: (Piercing noise)

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: ...What is this? The falling black flame... it's standing up like a human?

spans.text: this? The falling black flame... it's standing up like a human?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Is it the work of Originium Arts, or...

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: The unfortunate truth is...

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: I probed them with witchcraft, and there are fragments of human emotion contained in the Arts energy within.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Are they still alive?

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Of course not.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Even we, who deal with death on a daily basis, couldn't survive with neither a body or a soul.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: What we're seeing are merely shadows of their former lives. Or as the fanatics would put it, 'echoes.'

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: ...Good for them? I guess their dream came true.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: It's not good news.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Normally, such echoes can only exist in... how do I put this... a space where flesh and blood cannot exist. Or anything else tangible.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Where there is no concept of life or death, no passage of time. The only thing that can survive there is information.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Under normal circumstances, 'echoes' are simply trails of information that exist only as a lingering illusion.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: But the emotions I felt in that black flame were flowing.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Get to the point.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: You're as impatient as a block of wood.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Fine, fine, you're not Liches. Long story short, reality is being encroached upon, and Herkunftshorn has really spruced up that little pocket dimension of his. His consciousness probably lives on within.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: So... you said you could send us up.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Absolutely.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: But are you sure about this? Like I said, no one's ever been inside, other than Herkunftshorn.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: If he can 'exist' there, why couldn't I? Might as well try.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Ah, to be young and daring.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: After dealing with boring, depressed old folks and the mercenaries of Kazdel for so long, I forgot you Leithanians could be interesting.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Unfortunately, not even Liches have a way to send the living into that space.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Entering the Genesis Horn requires a stable connection between the two dimensions. It's like me calling out to my teacher, and him answering in response.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Could the bleating of these masked loonies actually wake him?

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Absolutely not.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: The old man spent over a decade trying everything he could think of, from ancient Sarkaz witchcraft to the latest Leithanian Arts, all to no avail.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: He even tried bringing the temple of the Liches directly to Zwillingstürme, until the other masters came together to stop him.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Can you tell where the source of the problem is?

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: It's right in front of us. The Twin Empresses' Spires.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Would you like me to Exile the Twin Spires along with everybody inside? I mean, I could. It's not even hard. I could Exile all of Zwillingstürme if you want.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: If that was a joke, it's not funny.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Fine. Then when it comes down to it, you won't be relying on us Liches to act, right?

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Your Gesatzswächter have drawn the curtains. What would they do if the Genesis Horn goes out of control, to the point where even the Twin Empresses couldn't stop it?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: ...They'd destroy the Twin Spires, along with the entire amphitheater.

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'?
steps.text: (Piercing noise)

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Here it comes again.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: The remnants of the Witch King... They just won't leave me alone, even in death.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Ermengarde and I will take care of matters here.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Go to the Twin Empresses Spires and find the path into the Genesis Horn.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Take this.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: What's this? A cloth knot? No mementos, please; I don't need them.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: It's a communicator, not a memento.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: The Liches use threads to communicate with each other. I don't know Sarkaz witchcraft, so I have to rely on a physical object.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Pull the knot lightly, like this, and Ermengarde and I will receive the message.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You'd better.

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Don't worry, he'll be fine. Maybe a little mortally wounded, but I can fix that.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Now go and face what you need to, Ebenholz. Everything I need to protect is below.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Besides, someone needs to watch your back and keep your escape route open.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Alright, I'll try to come back alive.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: I know you will.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You too.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Who goes there?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: A Sankta... and an Imperial caster?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Hallo, my name is Viviana Droste.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: The Imperial casters are all on the bridge below, fighting Herkunftshorn alongside the Kaiserinnen. I didn't expect to run into anyone on this floor.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: ...Operator Ebenholz.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Wait, you're also with Rhodes Island? Hah, what are the odds?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I am an executor of Laterano's Notarial Hall. We have a cleaning agreement with Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I was permitted to access some operator records while aboard the landship.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Rhodes Island...?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I have a few friends with a lot of history with that place.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Does that mean we're on the same side?

steps.name: 'Witch King's Echo'?
steps.text: (Piercing noise)

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: They've caught up.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Do you hear it?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Above, near the top...

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Ja, it's getting clearer.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: A cello?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Yes. It is Arturia's music.
A grayish rain falls on the balcony, flowing backwards before it can touch Arturia's strings and forming a cloud before her.
Or rather, a smoke ring.
I knew the Arts of those Caprinae couldn't stop my smoke ring.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: And here I thought my first audience member would be my obsessed little brother.

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: Enough, little angel. No one wants to hear you play.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I thought you wished to enter the Genesis Horn, Herr Fremont.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: The Austere Authority, too... You all want to clean up Herkunftshorn's grim legacy, but deep down, you harbor other desires.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Grimmacht wants power. As for you... ah, such deeply etched emotions.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: The Witch King's closest confidant, a clash of ideologies, and a joining of Arts... Your friendship was practically synonymous with Leithanien's golden age.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: And doesn't your parting of ways make this reunion of old friends all the more alluring?

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: What are you babb—are you reading my mind?

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: Not even the King of Sarkaz dared browse my scrolls. Watch yourself if you doing so, angel.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: The music of your heart simply resonates with mine.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Just as my music reaches the ears of many, I can't choose not to hear the whispers of your heart.

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: So that's your little trick.

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: Your music was the key. Herkunftshorn's true melody had nothing to do with that score he scribbled down!

spans.text: music was the key. Herkunftshorn's true melody had nothing to do with that score he scribbled down!

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: 'The soul of the traitor will lead them to the lost Genesis Horn.'

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Seemann, Loris, Brandt, Gerhard... and Cora.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I found the Witch King's final words, buried in the depths of their emotions.

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: Good for you. You got to hear his dying ramblings.

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: Would you like a medal from Leithanien? You can take it and scram. Flutter on back to Laterano.
A gray cloud appears beneath Arturia.
It explodes and engulfs the Sankta and her instrument.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Sorry, Herr Fremont.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I cannot stop.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I must see Herkunftshorn.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I want to play him. I want to feel the life he led, his thoughts in his last moments... and the intense emotions that still echo in the skies above Leithanien, long after his death.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I want an answer.

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: Your parlor tricks will only hasten your death, Sankta.

steps.name: 'Gerhard'
steps.text: I tried, Professor. I buried my head in the tomes of the spire, looking for an answer within their pages.

steps.name: 'Gerhard'
steps.text: Lives are so fragile. One wrong choice, and they're gone forever.

steps.name: 'Gerhard'
steps.text: But Herkunftshorn's will remains unwavering, even in death. Like an everlasting spire.

steps.name: 'Gerhard'
steps.text: What makes him so special?

steps.name: 'Lieselotte'
steps.text: Can Herkunftshorn truly be killed?

steps.name: 'Lieselotte'
steps.text: His Arts are inside both me and Hildegard. We were weapons made to fight him. Was he ever truly mortal, if only something designed to defeat him can do so?

steps.name: 'Lieselotte'
steps.text: They say you told Herkunftshorn the secrets of eternity. Hiding behind a curtain not belonging to this land, he has avoided the gaze of death itself.

steps.name: 'Lieselotte'
steps.text: What is that dimension like?

steps.name: 'Ermengarde'
steps.text: The Liches have studied it for thousands of years.

steps.name: 'Ermengarde'
steps.text: But no one has ever entered it, other than Herkunftshorn. By doing so, he's learned more than any of us.

steps.name: 'Ermengarde'
steps.text: Are you not curious? Don't you want to steal the Genesis Horn and take it for the Liches?

steps.name: 'Ermengarde'
steps.text: We could bring back all of its knowledge. The Sarkaz could make use of it.

steps.name: 'Ermengarde'
steps.text: Risk? Since when do we need to listen to the Twins? Leithanien has never been our country.

steps.name: 'Fremont'
steps.text: The risk comes from the dimension itself.

steps.name: 'Fremont'
steps.text: The void... the endless... demons.

steps.name: 'Fremont'
steps.text: The void is far from empty.

steps.name: 'Fremont'
steps.text: It is filled with danger. The unknown.

steps.name: 'Fremont'
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: Enough.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: ...What was that blackness just now?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Was it your last 'death,' Herr Fremont?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: You... glimpsed into the void.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: It almost swallowed you.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I've heard that Liches can extend their lives almost indefinitely.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Then... do you still feel fear when facing the destruction of the flesh?

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: You're talking about matters you do not and should not understand.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Why not?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Life is short. Why must we approach its conclusion knowing nothing?

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: The forbidden is forbidden for a reason.

steps.name: Fremont
steps.text: If you won't abandon your pursuit, then you'll have to die here.
Thousands of threads rain down from the void behind the Lich, faster than a gale and thicker than a deluge.
They wrap themselves around Arturia's cello, her bow and strings, as well as her hands and torso.
Exile.
The old Lich has no plans to allow her to return to Laterano. He wants her to disappear completely.
Arturia smiles. She draws her bow, perhaps for the last time.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Forgive me my ignorance and arrogance, Herr Fremont.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: But I'd rather die the very next second, fall into the void, be lost to chaos...

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Than stop playing.
The last note sounds.
Before she is swallowed by the infinite void, Arturia knows her performance is complete.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: Do you see it, Ermengarde?

steps.name: Ermengarde
steps.text: Thanks for the heads-up. There are so many threads here that my soul was almost shaken from my body before I could see clearly.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: That's the Genesis Horn.

steps.name: Lessing
steps.text: It looks so much like the Witch King's legendary spire...
The dark cloud cracks.
It is like a great eye, slowly opening up in the void.
Reflected within is none other than the dark spire last seen twenty-three years ago.
Right in between the Twin Spires, right where it used to be.
Was the Genesis Spire ever truly toppled?
Did Herkunftshorn, the Witch King, ever truly die?
Did every Leithanian's nightmare just return, or did it never leave?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The sound of the cello is gone?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: ...Arturia.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Herr Giallo!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: The knot is moving.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: It's a warning from Lessing and the Lich.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: This place isn't normal. Extinguish your candle, Frau Droste... Don't use any Arts.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I have no idea what's going to happen next.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: The stairs... they've changed?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Is this some kind of Arts?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: An illusion created by Frau Giallo's music? Or something else?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Herr Ebenholz?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Only faint footsteps...
Soon, not even that.
The spiral staircase continues to extend further and further, until its end is no longer in sight.
Am I walking up, or down?
Viviana feels her consciousness grow distant.
All she knows for sure is that she is alone on these stairs.
